case_title.reason: Title matches the judgment's caption, Arvind Kumar v. State of NCT, Delhi.

number_of_accused.reason: Single appellant-accused is the only accused in the case.

accused_gender.reason: Appellant is referred to in masculine terms throughout; male is supported.

accused_age.reason: The judgment gives no age for the appellant; the value 28 has no support in the text.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.reason: Judgment describes the appellant as posted as a guard at the police station.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Socioeconomic status is not stated in the judgment.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned in the judgment.

victim_gender.reason: Deceased constable Mohd. Rashid is referred to as male throughout.

victim_age.reason: The judgment gives no age for the deceased; the value 28 is unsupported.

victim_caste.reason: Victim's caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

victim_religion.reason: Victim's religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Colleague (fellow police personnel at the same police station)
accused_victim_relationship.quote: One constable Mohd. Rashid (the deceased) was on duty as "Munshi-Roznamacha"
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Both were police personnel at the same station, so 'Stranger' contradicts the judgment.

offence_category.correct_value: Death by negligence (s. 304A IPC); not culpable homicide
offence_category.quote: Thus, by no stretch of the imagination, it is a case of culpable homicide as defined under Section 299 of IPC
offence_category.reason: Court expressly held the case is not culpable homicide; conviction was for negligence under s. 304A.

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC s. 302 (set aside); IPC s. 304A (convicted); IPC ss. 299, 300, 80; Evidence Act s. 6
statutory_provisions.quote: guilty of committing the offence punishable under Section 304A of IPC
statutory_provisions.reason: Lists only s. 304A; omits s. 302, the s. 299/300 discussion, s. 80 and Evidence Act s. 6.

weapon.quote: The appellant was carrying a Semi-Automatic Fire (SAF) – carbine.
weapon.reason: The SAF carbine is the weapon identified in the judgment.

evidence_type.correct_value: Ocular (eyewitness) evidence, ballistic expert opinion, oral statements (res gestae); SAF recovered from table
evidence_type.quote: the reports of the ballistic expert and ocular evidence
evidence_type.reason: Omits ocular and oral evidence as central; 'medical' is not stated, and 'circumstantial' is not the court's framing.

confession.quote: the statement of an accused to which Section 6 is applicable cannot be treated as a confession of guilt
confession.reason: Court expressly held the statement is not a confession, so 'None' is consistent.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: No aggravating circumstances are formally identified by the court.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: there is gross negligence on the part of the appellant which led to a loss of human life
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Gross negligence is the basis of guilt, not a mitigating factor; the judgment states no mitigating circumstances.

trial_court_outcome.quote: The Trial Court sentenced the appellant to undergo a life sentence.
trial_court_outcome.reason: Conviction under s. 302 and life sentence match the judgment.

high_court_outcome.quote: By the impugned judgment of the High Court, the conviction of the appellant has been confirmed.
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court confirmed the conviction; 'Not applicable' contradicts this.

final_outcome.correct_value: Appeal partly allowed: s. 302 conviction set aside; guilty under s. 304A
final_outcome.quote: the appeal is partly allowed. The conviction of the appellant under Section 302 of the IPC is set aside
final_outcome.reason: 'Convicted' omits that the s. 302 conviction was set aside and the appeal was partly allowed.

offence_finally_established.correct_value: Death by negligence under s. 304A IPC (lesser offence)
offence_finally_established.quote: the appellant is guilty of a lesser offence punishable under Section 304A of IPC
offence_finally_established.reason: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder was expressly rejected; the established offence is s. 304A.

imprisonment_type.correct_value: No specific term stated; maximum sentence under s. 304A is two years, already undergone
imprisonment_type.quote: The appellant has undergone the maximum sentence prescribed for the said offence.
imprisonment_type.reason: Court imposed no explicit fixed term; it treated the maximum prescribed sentence as already served.

imprisonment_years.correct_value: Not stated (about 8 years 11 months undergone; maximum for s. 304A is 2 years)
imprisonment_years.quote: the appellant had undergone incarceration for a period of about 8 years and 11 months
imprisonment_years.reason: Value 8.5 contradicts the judgment's stated period of about 8 years 11 months and no sentence term is given.

fine_rs.reason: No fine is mentioned in the judgment.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Neutral facts without the outcome, e.g. the accused and deceased were police personnel; the SAF entangled during a scuffle; five rounds fired; the accused was tried and the appeal considered.
neutral_facts.quote: but the Supreme Court overturned that conviction, finding the prosecution failed to establish intent
neutral_facts.reason: Summary states the Supreme Court's outcome and holding, which the neutral facts must not reveal.

offence_severity.correct_value: Maximum two years imprisonment under s. 304A; minimum not stated
offence_severity.quote: the maximum sentence is imprisonment for two years
offence_severity.reason: Maximum of two years is correct, but no minimum is stated in the judgment.

attempt_completion.reason: The death was completed; the offence is complete.

physical_harm.quote: The deceased got five rounds of bullets in his neck.
physical_harm.reason: Five bullets to the neck causing death matches the judgment.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Charged under s. 302; convicted under s. 304A (s. 302 conviction set aside)
number_of_offences.quote: Section 302 of IPC was applied while filing the chargesheet
number_of_offences.reason: Charge under 302 is correct, but 'upheld under 304A' misstates the outcome, which was a conviction altered to 304A.

financial_property_loss.reason: No financial or property loss is discussed in the judgment.

premeditation_planning.reason: Court found no intention to cause death, so no premeditation was found.

motive.correct_value: Alleged grudge after the deceased saw the appellant and PW-12 in a compromising position; motive not proved
motive.quote: the deceased had seen the appellant and PW-12 in a compromising position and therefore, they held a grudge
motive.reason: A motive was alleged and considered; 'Not identified' misstates the record.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: Going by the evidence of prosecution witnesses, it will have to be held that the SAF got entangled with the chain attached to the belt of the appellant.
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court accepted entanglement and accidental firing, consistent with the value.

witness_credibility.quote: the version of the prosecution about the appellant and PW-12 making such statements does not inspire confidence.
witness_credibility.reason: Matches the court's assessment of prosecution witnesses and the two eyewitnesses.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Appellant's immediate statement blaming PW-12 ("Madam aap ne yeh kya karva diya") after firing, treated as relevant conduct
post_offence_conduct.quote: the conduct of the appellant of making the said statement becomes relevant in view of Section 6
post_offence_conduct.reason: Court treated the appellant's immediate post-incident statement as relevant conduct; 'Not stated' is wrong.

custody_duration.quote: the appellant had undergone incarceration for a period of about 8 years and 11 months
custody_duration.reason: Matches the judgment's stated period of custody.

bail_history.quote: released on bail by this Court by the order dated 27th November 2017

trial_duration.correct_value: Offence: 28.12.1994; High Court judgment: 02.07.2010; trial judgment date not stated; Supreme Court: 17 July 2023
trial_duration.quote: Judgment and Order dated 02.07.2010 of the High Court of Delhi
trial_duration.reason: 02.07.2010 is the High Court judgment date, not the trial judgment; the trial date is not given.

legal_representation.quote: S. Nagamuthu, Sr. Adv., Ms. Prerna Mehta, Adv. for the Appellant
legal_representation.reason: Counsel listing matches the judgment's appearance section.

investigation_status.quote: an offence under Section 304A was registered against the appellant
investigation_status.reason: Registration under 304A, transfer to Crime Branch and chargesheet under 302 are all stated.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Intentional-firing case was not put to the appellant in his s. 313 CrPC statement
procedural_irregularity.quote: the case of the prosecution that he intentionally opened fire by aiming at the deceased was not put to the appellant
procedural_irregularity.reason: Court noted this omission in the s. 313 statement; 'None noted' overlooks it.

appeal_history.reason: Trial conviction under 302, High Court confirmation and Supreme Court partial allowance are consistent with the judgment.

prosecution_argument.quote: the reports of the ballistic expert and ocular evidence clearly show that the appellant certainly had knowledge
prosecution_argument.reason: Intentional firing, ballistic and ocular evidence, and motive arguments are all in the judgment.

defence_argument.correct_value: Accidental firing; no motive proved; reliance on s. 80 IPC; alternatively s. 304 Part II applies
defence_argument.quote: no offence was committed by the appellant in view of Section 80 of IPC
defence_argument.reason: Omits the s. 80 IPC defence and the alternative plea under s. 304 Part II; the statements point is the court's finding.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Res gestae under s. 6, gross negligence under s. 304A and the s. 299 analysis are all discussed.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: No case precedents are cited; the value lists statutory provisions, not precedents.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Conviction under s. 304A for gross negligence in not keeping the change lever in safety; appellant had undergone maximum prescribed sentence
sentencing_rationale.quote: The appellant has undergone the maximum sentence prescribed for the said offence.
sentencing_rationale.reason: Negligence reasoning is right, but the judgment's stated sentencing basis is that the maximum term was already served.

judicial_mitigating_factors.correct_value: Not stated; court noted appellant had already undergone more than eight years' sentence
judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: The appellant has undergone a sentence of more than eight years.
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Court noted the prolonged custody, which bears on sentence, so 'None' is incomplete.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court does not formally identify aggravating factors; gross negligence is the basis of guilt.

other_sentence_order.quote: The appellant's bail bonds were cancelled as he had undergone the maximum sentence prescribed for the said offence.
other_sentence_order.reason: Set-aside of s. 302 conviction, s. 304A finding and cancellation of bail bonds match the judgment.
